world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Levy 1978, 'Costanoan', Handbook of North American Indians vol. 8 — phonological sketch plausibly covers stress; not online. Kroeber 1910 (archive.org) was read: no stress statement

sources.citation: Powell, J. W. 1877. Appendix: Linguistics. In Stephen Powers, Tribes of California (Contributions to North American Ethnology 3), 439-613. Washington: GPO.
sources.note: Prints the Mengarini 'Santa Clara' (Tamyen) vocabulary (no. 6, p. 536) with Gibbs's orthographic note on vowels and consonants only; the only accent remark is Powell's general recommendation to mark 'the principal [syllable] with an accent, thus: Da-ko'-ta' (a transcription convention). No Tamyen/Costanoan stress statement.
sources.venue: Stephen Powers, Tribes of California (Contributions to North American Ethnology 3)

sources.citation: Golla, Victor. 2011. California Indian Languages. Berkeley: University of California Press (Costanoan section, ch. 3.20).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011 FOLIO; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011) (also lendable online at archive.org; also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011 FOLIO; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011
sources.note: Standard survey of the family with a phonological note per language; may report Chochenyo stress second-hand from Harrington/Beeler.

sources.citation: Milliken, Randall, Laurence H. Shoup & Beverly R. Ortiz. 2009. Ohlone/Costanoan Indians of the San Francisco Peninsula and their Neighbors, Yesterday and Today. Oakland: Archaeological and Historical Consultants (report for NPS Golden Gate NRA).
sources.note: Ch. 2 'Native Languages of West-Central California' (pp. 25-36) reviews classification (Kroeber 1904/1910, Beeler 1961, Levy 1976, Callaghan, Blevins & Golla 2005) and quotes Callaghan on Chochenyo/Ramaytush/Tamyen morphology; Appendix A gives Harrington Chochenyo interview excerpts (ethnogeography). No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Harrington, John P. 1921-1929. Chochenyo field notes (José Guzmán, Angela Colos). National Anthropological Archives; microfilm reels in Mills (ed.), The Papers of John Peabody Harrington, vol. 2; images at CLA Berkeley (bndlid=1024).
sources.note: The only substantial primary record of Chochenyo speech; Harrington marks accent in his transcriptions, so any stress rule would have to be extracted from these notes (or from Blevins's unpublished Chochenyo grammar sketches for the Muwekma tribe).
sources.venue: The Papers of John Peabody Harrington

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1910. The Chumash and Costanoan Languages. University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 9(2): 237-271.
sources.note: Costanoan 'Phonetics' pp. 249-251 (vowels u o a e i; stops k t. t p; San Jose = Chochenyo consonant distribution) and 'Grammatical notes: San Jose' pp. 251 ff. contain no statement on stress or accent; a full-text search for stress/accent finds only the non-linguistic 'accentuated'.
sources.venue: University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology

sources.citation: California Language Archive (Survey of California and Other Indian Languages), language pages 'Chochenyo', 'Ramaytush', 'Tamyen'.
sources.note: Descriptions and further-reading lists only (Beeler 1961, 1972; Brown 1973; Hinton 2001; Okrand 1991; Levy 1976; Golla 2011; Heizer 1952, 1955; Kroeber 1910; Milliken et al. 2009); Ramaytush 'only attested in a few wordlists', Tamyen 'clearly attested only in a single wordlist recorded by Gregory Mengarini'. Nothing on stress.
Chochenyo phonology section gives consonant/vowel tables and vowel length (oo = /o:/); nothing on stress or accent; references are press items and the Harrington notes catalogue entry.

sources.citation: Levy, Richard. 1978. Costanoan. In Robert F. Heizer (ed.), Handbook of North American Indians, vol. 8: California, 485-495. Washington: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Named by an earlier compilation as the source; HNAI chapters carry an orthographic/phonological footnote that may state stress placement for Costanoan (Chochenyo forms).

sources.citation: Beeler, Madison S. 1961. Northern Costanoan. International Journal of American Linguistics 27(3): 191-197.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only published grammatical/phonological sketch of Chochenyo (Northern Costanoan), based on Arroyo de la Cuesta's and Harrington's materials; the most likely place for a stress statement on this language.

sources.citation: Callaghan, Catherine A. 2014. Proto Utian Grammar and Dictionary, with Notes on Yokuts. Trends in Linguistics Documentation 31. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM1977.C35 2014)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM1977 .C35 2014
sources.note: Comparative grammar of Costanoan and Miwok with Chochenyo/Harrington data; the grammar part (pp. 68-203) is the modern authority on Costanoan phonology including accent/vowel length.

sources.citation: Blevins, Juliette. 2005. Origins of Northern Costanoan shak:en 'six': A reconsideration of senary counting in Utian. International Journal of American Linguistics 71(1): 87-101.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Blevins is the linguist who analysed Harrington's Chochenyo notes for the Muwekma revitalization; her IJAL papers give Chochenyo forms with phonological commentary and may note stress.

sources.citation: Levy, Richard L. 1976. Costanoan internal relationships. Berkeley: Archaeological Research Facility, Department of Anthropology, University of California. 57 pp., map (cover title; bibliography pp. 54-56).

sources.note: Record and secondary summary only: HathiTrust/Harvard MARC (57 p., map, subject 'Ohlone language') and Milliken, Shoup & Ortiz 2009: 31-32, who summarise it as a statistical re-evaluation of Costanoan subgrouping from shared lexical, phonological and semantic innovations, concluding a dialect chain with a northern subgroup (San Francisco/Ramaytush, East Bay/Chochenyo, Santa Clara/Tamyen) versus a southern one (quoting Levy 1976: 38); the phonological evidence is segmental correspondences as far as can be seen; nothing on stress, accent or tone is visible and Costanoan is nowhere reported tona…
